content.user_title: Model BDI Mental States from RDF
content.value_statement: Teams building cognitive agents need a clear way to map context into beliefs, desires, and intentions. This skill provides ontology patterns, RDF examples, SPARQL checks, and integration guidance for traceable BDI modeling.
actual_capabilities: Defines BDI classes for beliefs, desires, intentions, mental processes, plans, world states, and justifications.
Maps external RDF context into belief, desire, and intention chains.
Provides Turtle examples for workflows, multi-agent coordination, conflicts, and payment processing.
Includes SPARQL competency queries for validation, temporal checks, and traceability.
Shows integration patterns for SEMAS, LAG pipelines, JADE, JADEX, triple stores, and FIPA ACL.
limitations: It is documentation and modeling guidance, not an executable BDI engine.
It does not validate RDF automatically unless users implement the referenced checks.
Framework examples require adaptation to project libraries and ontology versions.
It does not provide domain-specific policies for accepting or rejecting intentions.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Mental-State Schemas
use_cases.description: Use the BDI class and property patterns to structure beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, and justifications.

use_cases.title: Build RDF-to-BDI Pipelines
use_cases.description: Translate external RDF context into cognitive state objects before LLM reasoning or agent planning.

use_cases.title: Validate Multi-Agent Reasoning
use_cases.description: Use SPARQL competency queries to inspect shared beliefs, temporal validity, conflicts, and coordinated intentions.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Context as BDI States
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this RDF or text context, identify candidate world states, beliefs, desires, and intentions. Explain each mapping briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Create Turtle BDI Triples
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the following context into Turtle using the BDI ontology. Include world states, beliefs, desires, intentions, temporal validity, and justifications.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a BDI Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Turtle graph against the BDI competency questions. List missing fulfilment, motivation, support, temporal, and justification links.

prompt_templates.title: Design Framework Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an integration that maps this BDI ontology model into my agent framework. Cover storage, reasoning, SPARQL validation, and message exchange.

output_examples.input: A meeting starts at 10:00, the room is confirmed, and an assistant must prepare notes.
output: World state: confirmed meeting time and room.
Belief: the meeting is scheduled and location is known.
Intention: create notes before the meeting with room and time as support.

output_examples.input: A BDI graph has intentions but no fulfilment links to desires.
output_examples.output: The review should flag each intention without a fulfilled desire, then suggest adding explicit fulfilment links and supporting beliefs.

output_examples.input: Two agents report conflicting locations for the same package.
output: Model each location report as a belief with its source and time.
Represent the conflict with justifications, then select a resolved intention using current evidence.

best_practices: Model world states independently from agent beliefs so multiple agents can hold different perspectives.
Attach time intervals and justifications to every important mental state.
Run competency queries after each graph update to catch missing motivation and fulfilment links.
anti_patterns: Do not treat raw observations as beliefs without a world-state reference.
Do not commit intentions directly to actions without a plan and task structure.
Do not omit temporal validity when beliefs may change over time.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides modeling guidance, examples, and validation patterns for BDI mental-state design.

faq.question: Can it generate RDF triples?
faq.answer: It can guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to draft Turtle triples from context. Users should validate the graph.

faq.question: What ontology does it use?
faq.answer: It uses a BDI ontology pattern with beliefs, desires, intentions, mental processes, world states, plans, time, and justifications.

faq.question: Is it useful without SPARQL?
faq.answer: Yes. SPARQL queries provide the clearest way to test graph completeness and explainability.

faq.question: Which agent frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The references discuss SEMAS, Logic Augmented Generation, JADE, JADEX, triple stores, and FIPA ACL messaging.

faq.question: What should users provide?
faq.answer: Provide the domain context, known world states, agent goals, temporal data, and any evidence behind each mental state.
